made_by: Visual lane (Claude), 3 Nov 2026, Blender 4.2.3 LTS, procedural build; no Meshy, no external assets
reference: Drafted reference (text): a crowned stone gateway for the Stormwood. Four legs of stacked, stratified slate (dark grey-violet, horizontal strata) on mossy root-stone feet, joined by four pointed arches of dressed voussoirs so that an arch faces every approach; a verdigris copper band two thirds up each leg and a copper-capped keystone on each arch; a stone crown ring over the crossing carrying five pale-blue glowing glass points, the tallest reaching 7 m. Palette per the Stormwood board: storm slate, cool moss, copper-patina green and glass highlights. No red or oxblood (earlier judges flagged red-brown bands). Answers the judges' 'an authored arch, two pillars and a spanning crown, seated into the moss'.
scale_check: source/scale_check.jpg: the arch beside a 1.80 m cylinder (the trainer). Legs at +-2.15 m leave a 3.4 m clear opening on both axes (the passage trigger is 2.2 x 2.5 m); arch spring 3.7 m, apex 5.35 m, crown points to 7.0 m, about 3.9x the trainer.
textures: Baked from procedural Cycles materials (packed 1024 albedo); glass uses an emissive material

revisions.reference: Drafted reference (text), F41#17 close-out from the judges' remaining asks: the same four-legged crowned arch and passage; the stone weathered (vertical rain streaks, olive-ochre lichen patches) instead of one uniform lilac; more copper (a second lower band on each leg, copper straps across each arch) and two pale-blue glass shards set into each leg; the landing's flagstones step down and bed into the ground toward a ragged edge, moss in the gaps, and a ring of half-sunk rubble and moss mounds buries the 9 x 9 m footing's square edge. No red or oxblood.
